note: Thesis-driven NOMINATION store — the top of the stacked funnel. Names here were nominated by JUDGMENT (Claude, thesis-review agent, or the user), not by the data screen. Nomination is not endorsement: every name still flows through the SAME factor rank + hard screen as the rest of the universe (see .claude/agents/scout.md). A name that fails the hard data screen is FLAGGED with its reason and buyable only as a logged override (never a silent pass). `risk_tag` is the SUBJECTIVE risk read; it is kept separate from the objective data_risk_score the ranker computes. STALENESS: theses are dated and rest on Claude's training knowledge (cutoff Jan 2026) unless a number is fetched in-session; treat the qualitative thesis as an analyst view to verify, not fetched fact. Tickers here must also be added to universe.json category `thesis_candidates` via scripts/add_manual_tickers.py (validated).

candidates.name: Schneider Electric
candidates.thesis: Electrification + data-center power demand (the 'shovel' of the AI build-out) + energy-efficiency, all policy-funded. Quality compounder with pricing power; genuinely sustainability-aligned (its product IS efficiency, not a bolt-on label). Fits the user's Europe + sustainability + growth preference. Highest-conviction of this set.
candidates.policy_tailwind: Western grid-buildout and energy-transition spending; data-center power demand.
candidates.rationale_risk: Cyclical industrial, rarely cheap — entry valuation matters; not a defensive holding.

candidates.name: ASML Holding
candidates.thesis: Effective monopoly on EUV lithography — no advanced chip exists without its machines. Wide moat, high margins, secular semiconductor demand.
candidates.policy_tailwind: US CHIPS Act + EU Chips Act reshoring subsidies drive fab build-out.
candidates.rationale_risk: Cyclical order book; China export-restriction exposure is a real swing factor.

candidates.name: Infineon Technologies
candidates.thesis: European power-semiconductor leader levered to EV and industrial electrification — sustainability-adjacent growth.
candidates.rationale_risk: Tied to the auto cycle; more cyclical/volatile than the others here.

candidates.name: Iberdrola
candidates.thesis: Renewables-heavy regulated utility — a real sustainability holding and a steadier ballast within the medium tier.
candidates.rationale_risk: Rate-sensitive and capital-intensive; lower growth than the rest — the 'ballast' pick.

candidates.name: Novo Nordisk
candidates.thesis: GLP-1 (obesity/diabetes) structural demand; dominant franchise, high margins.
candidates.policy_tailwind: Drug-pricing politics run AGAINST this one (US pricing pressure) — a headwind, flagged honestly.
candidates.rationale_risk: HIGH STALENESS RISK: Novo was in real turmoil around the Jan-2026 knowledge cutoff (GLP-1 competition, mixed trial readouts). Verify current fundamentals before trusting this thesis — it is the least reliable name on the list.

candidates.name: Taiwan Semiconductor (US ADR)
candidates.thesis: The foundry essentially all advanced chips depend on; scale and process-node lead form a deep moat.
candidates.policy_tailwind: Reshoring subsidies (CHIPS Act) fund its US fabs.
candidates.rationale_risk: Taiwan geopolitical risk is the dominant, non-diversifiable tail. Files 20-F not 10-K, so SEC fundamentals won't populate — will rank momentum-only.
